answer: Before an agent can earn reputation, it must lock a scarce stake and pass a randomized challenge tied to a recurring pulse of activity; one identity cannot reuse the same proof, since each challenge binds a fresh cipher to its stake and prior history. Honest agents recover the stake over time, while a fake fleet must fund every account separately and risks forfeiting funds when caught. Splitting one stake across many marble-thin identities therefore buys little influence and makes attacks costly.
